hepta4800.head: 1b390853e50aa2fdae2e6c68793f94742d2d667c
hepta4800.body_snapshot:
## Problem

An actual source-built Asterinas run of the unchanged A39 owner failed before initial activation: guest PID 2 (Manager), syscall 42 (connect), errno 13, at guest 8.215 s. At that point the Manager's only connection is its original launch endpoint, and the state disk remained byte-identical to its preimage. The bound pathname was published before the original chown/chmod completed. Asterinas initially creates this socket file with mode 0600.

The complete diagnosis is retained in [Desktop PR #293](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/trillionnium-os-desktop/pull/293), canonical Desktop `c42eccaf8b9b5a163d0c52b1a3c42466fe0f425b`, durable desktop job `1a1a6fdf770-fc05-29c9`. All five original scenarios ran: three refusal controls passed; both positive scenarios failed. The second positive had no EACCES and instead returned Unavailable during initial activation, so it remains a distinct blocker.

## Changes

The first commit changes the existing shared native listener factory to retain a private PublishedListener:

- Bind a pending basename in the same verified Root-controlled parent, refusing collisions without pre-unlink.
- Apply the original Root/group/0660 custody and nonblocking mode before publishing the final name.
- Publish with renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) against the held parent directory fd. There is no ordinary-rename fallback.
- Require the pending name to disappear and the final name to refer to the exact recorded socket filesystem device/inode, Root UID, expected group and mode.
- Retain inode custody until listener drop. Failed or completed cleanup removes only the matching socket inode, preserving foreign pending/final names and replacement inodes.

The actual c42 Asterinas implementation supports NOREPLACE and keeps the inode identity across a same-directory RamFs rename. Its same-inode-alias early-success edge is handled by the explicit pending-name-disappeared postcondition. The original native peer channels continue to verify SO_PEERCRED and held pidfds; these particular channels do not authenticate a pathname returned by getsockname.

The second commit retains bounded startup context on errors: a fixed phase enum and optional numeric errno. It preserves the original error internally without logging paths, buffers or the underlying error payload. Successful calls add no diagnostic output.

## Validation and remaining execution

- Both local stages passed the original just fmt recipe and git diff --check.
- An independent source review checked publication, same-inode alias handling, field drop order and cleanup boundaries.
- Six explicit Root fixtures cover real dedicated-UID connectivity, pending collision, final collision, replacement inodes and a pre-existing same-inode alias. They use the existing HEPTA_SOCKET_TEST_ROOT fixture convention and are explicitly ignored by the ordinary unprivileged suite. They have not yet run.
- The actual corrected-owner production binary compiled and packaged on rog; the first measured ELF was refused by the original image gates, as recorded below. Clippy, the six actual host-Root fixtures and the new source-bound native five-boot chain remain pending.
- No dependency, retry error set, native deadline or resource policy was changed. Physical material remains 500 ms; guest remains 1 CPU / 512 MiB; each original boot remains bounded by 120 s.

The pathname safety argument relies on the verified Root-only-writable ancestry and original Root serialization. It does not claim protection from a concurrent privileged Root replacing the entire parent. An indeterminate metadata error after a successful rename fails closed and may retain the final name; it does not trigger a blind unlink or retry.


## Actual corrected-owner measurement on rog

The unchanged canonical `6b715d2c92ce8ab74f0829ce6926fe8dfc8d7f5f` source was built by the original locked/offline GNU `crt-static` release command and packaged by the original release script. No feature or release profile was changed.

- Durable job: `1a1a75e66f9-fc05-2b24`, started 2026-11-04 16:22:25 UTC and completed 16:56:22 UTC.
- The original Cargo build returned 0 after 2033.128 s and original packaging returned 0. The original legacy-shape builder returned **1**, with `static initial ELF size out of bounds`. The outer measurement process returned 0 only because measurement and preservation completed; this is not an admission or native pass.
- Packaged ELF SHA-256: `72ef211b5989c9a240ec92582afbbc1dd1154d0001ac5851c9fc994cb21d4cf0`.
- Measured F = **20,285,048 B**, L = **20,316,160 B**, S = **15,454,208 B**, with exactly four LOAD segments. These exceed the unchanged A39 ceilings by **146,464 / 147,456 / 131,072 B**, respectively. This candidate was refused before kernel/guest execution.
- Original builder receipt SHA-256: `95499c1b8631bef9e685c949eca97731340d3e4275fced4a91f18b33f9eb6b42`.
- Preserved measurement receipt: `/home/qian-qi/work/trill-g2-native-rog-20261104-v1/receipts/owner-measurement-6b715-v1.json`, SHA-256 `732f1eeb5592ea6dc499979dece6dc16180ce647013e4bc3f86e2866d95a9b66`.

That first host used GCC 15/glibc 2.43, while the original desktop used GCC 13.3/glibc 2.39. Actual symbol evidence shows changed libc/libgcc and unchanged-source SQLite function sizes; it does not assign the entire size difference to any one cause. The comparison receipt SHA-256 is `ba52271f173e8f00bbfb3336a77b6ecff6d71e582935d68aa26a295b30cf4b68`.

Before another build, a private Ubuntu 24.04 environment was prepared without changing the host compiler, dpkg state or permissions. **84 original tool/library paths matched their desktop SHA-256 values**, including GCC/cc1, Clang/libclang, CMake, binutils, glibc/static runtimes and their recorded dynamic dependencies. Original input-manifest SHA-256: `4562cd88aa24694ccf5eb639c1c1700f587b6500253c11b4a5ad2d8c790a464e`; completed identity receipt SHA-256: `0c0806abda17a3ce256859bc44c0ec7706a1a51f5eb989a2b424e7a165c4139d`.

The same c42/6b pair completed its independent cold build in the read-only matched GNU environment. Durable job `1a1a7b4ad16-fc05-2c55` ran from 17:56:39 to 18:32:26 UTC: original Cargo returned 0 after 2136.565 s, original packaging returned 0, and the original legacy-shape builder returned **1** (`static initial ELF size out of bounds`). The outer measurement again returned 0 only for preserved measurement. Its ELF SHA-256 is `4020a9477086202d1fb18745419bc77dc669695d309e6de14a5f8ffae71df0d1`; F/L/S are **20,179,992 / 20,209,664 / 15,351,808 B**, still **41,408 / 40,960 / 28,672 B** above unchanged A39 limits. Four LOAD segments remain. No new guest ran.

The original builder receipt SHA-256 is `05449a933a7e2e72910013011db4a01e966562101199881e3b39f142134f417f`; preserved measurement receipt `receipts/owner-measurement-6b715-gnu24-v1.json` has SHA-256 `ad9f52073b67055171d69d52e13e2c45b523a1c9bf09c8ddc9e004a62284773d`. After the build, all 84 original GNU file hashes matched again. Observed successful tool executions and static archive/CRT opens plus 22,744 trace-file hashes are retained in `gnu24-run-v1/post-link-provenance-v1.json`, SHA-256 `1f991aa303f128231f846aa1f08d745025625c1a13f681bdd75bfdda81e67a09`. The trace did not record clone ancestry, so this is not asserted to be a complete per-thread final-link closure.

## Narrow code-size candidate, awaiting actual measurement

Actual section comparison found .text +30,016 B and .rodata +12,416 B. The same 530 embedded Rust source paths occupy 8,938 additional bytes in the longer rog cache/toolchain paths; that is a bounded path accounting, not complete attribution of the ELF difference. Both .comment sections identify the same Rust 1.96, LLD 22.1.2 and GCC 13.3 toolchains.

Actual symbols show three distinct generated `owner::execute` poll bodies in both binaries: 156,508 visible bytes in A39 and 152,082 in the corrected matched-GNU build. This function itself became smaller; its existing duplication is an optimization opportunity, not the claimed source of the size increase. The third commit only adds `#[inline(never)]` and an explanatory comment to this private async function. The command body remains byte-for-byte unchanged, preserving all commands, authority checks, original budgets, atomic publication and all 13 diagnostic stages. This compiler hint may or may not eliminate duplication; only a new actual ELF can establish the effect.

Original `just fmt` and `git diff --check` passed for this two-line candidate. Its canonical head is `1b390853e50aa2fdae2e6c68793f94742d2d667c`, tree `14a9e4ef975734cd9416014f6d0a11bca50599e4`. The pending new source-bound measurement will reuse this task's idle GNU24 target and preserve all original build flags, limits and prior failed artifacts. No capacity or runtime success is claimed for this head.

No A39 F/L/S ceiling, physical-material deadline, guest limit or original build command has been enlarged. A matching environment alone grants no image or runtime qualification.

## Source identity and evidence boundary

This draft targets the existing frozen A39 base branch `codex/desktop-organ-base-a39-20261103` at `a39a0871d9601ffccb5e0d95d8f39d54b3a63360`. It can be cherry-picked into the separately reviewed joint lifecycle tree, whose runtime evidence must be produced for that exact combined source.

- Canonical custody commit: `5e469453bb9bbb5d1f0df124878f1ddbfe260834`, tree `1e852504b4d5d81ebfb30a2d81a2ed17a8fcc2bd`.
- Canonical diagnostic-context commit: `6b715d2c92ce8ab74f0829ce6926fe8dfc8d7f5f`, tree `9a2cd2d45201a81ecac9be37536d0a125296c22c`.
- The two original published trees and the new poll-hint tree exactly match the independently checked local stage trees.
- Prior A39 ELF SHA-256 `6ce96a0785b2cbb51bb71fabb2973c1e04d93e213d56694b42b4d717ed55a454` remains the preserved failing original input. The corrected owner requires a newly measured ELF and a new explicitly bound source/image profile; it cannot inherit A39 runtime eligibility.
- Original five-boot diagnosis SHA-256: `74ad0dc5d2218cb0b378632a1cd5b225fb6b7fb69c443490e56e0882ff70cb7a`.

No production or full-G2 qualification is claimed by this draft.

hepta4803.body_snapshot:
## Why

The original `14e2d89b3367232ec5dbe6187f09feed0f2b68d3` source already resolves and verifies the Codex-published Rusty V8 archive and matching Rust binding. The local helper audit invoked Cargo directly, so it missed that existing resolver and fell through to the upstream sandbox archive URL, which returned 404. This change makes the supported local entry explicit and reusable.

This draft has an exact review base at `14e2d89b3367232ec5dbe6187f09feed0f2b68d3` on `codex/v8-local-cargo-resolver-base-14e-20261104`. It does not target `main`.

## Changes

- Add `--run COMMAND...` to the existing `scripts/hepta_ci_v8.py` entry. It delegates version selection, download, and checksum verification to the existing `codex_package.v8` resolver; validates the complete archive/binding pair before starting the child; and runs the original argv in `codex-rs` with the resolved environment.
- Preserve the existing no-argument `GITHUB_ENV` export mode.
- Extend the existing tests from 6 to 10. The positive forwarding case launches a real temporary Python child, observes its actual cwd, argv and the three relevant environment values, and verifies normal exit status 17. The resolver is mocked in this unit test to avoid a network dependency.
- Document local usage and the verified release provenance in the existing `third_party/v8/README.md`. The normal-exit guarantee does not claim preservation of POSIX signal termination status.

No Cargo manifest, lockfile, Rust feature, profile, original helper command, or App Server test assertion is changed. Both commits belong to this review: `eac45e60299495186747965ea0020f7be0c523a9` then `83ad164ff05cb34d444d51e23ee286fa0241c783`.

## Actual validation

- All **10/10** existing and added Python tests passed, including the real child process exit-17 case.
- Original `just fmt`: exit 0.
- `git diff --check`: exit 0.
- Final validation receipt: `/home/qq/work/trill-v8-1504-sandbox-prereq-20261104-r1/local-launcher-real-child-v2/result.json`, SHA-256 `2e1c59058919394b2c2c8f434025a77b909aa61491bdf1db8356b6f3db4b2d40`; durable job `1a1a7c90c2e-fc05-2c8a` exited 0.
- Independently, the **unmodified frozen 14e resolver** downloaded and verified all three original release files. This was a separate preparation run, not a Rust helper or App Server pass. Its receipt is `/data/trill-four-package-14e-20261104-v4/original-v8-resolver/result.json`, SHA-256 `f9ef851ac484e736a2c4287f2344d234559d9d63598e2296c910601dc9bb5461`; durable job `1a1a7b39b58-fc05-2c50` exited 0.

The verified dependency source is [openai/codex rusty-v8-v150.4.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rusty-v8-v150.4.0), release ID **361445880** (`prerelease=true`, not a Denoland-published binary). The original GNU target is `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; the original resolved features are `default`, `use_custom_libcxx`, `v8_enable_pointer_compression`, and `v8_enable_sandbox`.

| `librusty_v8_ptrcomp_sandbox_release_x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.a.gz` | 29,366,352 | `a35c75d1f26e6a983885a45b33490a4ebe54f05050568b32b89cfb421b30b583` |

## Qualification boundaries and retained failures

The original helper/App Server continuation remains pending; these Python tests and dependency hashes do **not** establish that it passes. The unchanged clean 14e source, original test parameters, target lease and resource gates remain the basis for that execution.

The independent Ubuntu 24.04 / Rust 1.96.0 source-build fallback is **not qualified**. Its real run reached the original V8 build script but failed before GN generation while downloading the pinned GN CIPD tool (`Network is unreachable`); Cargo exited 101 and the outer job exited 2. No archive or binding pair was produced. The original 404 failure and this separate source-build failure are retained, and the README does not present the fallback as a validated recipe.

desktop293.head: c42eccaf8b9b5a163d0c52b1a3c42466fe0f425b
desktop293.body_snapshot:
## Problem

The original A39 owner was built and packaged on Desktop `35ce124c3d54953cfc23cd89341fb7b51d5a3c01`, followed by a source-built kernel and all five unchanged native scenarios. Three refusal controls passed; both positive scenarios failed. Remaining per-Bio and per-IRQ INFO logging produced 3,593 messages in the steady-state boot, while the first userspace permission failure lacked the failing PID and syscall.

## Changes

- Move the per-Bio request dump and per-block IRQ message to the existing OSTD debug level.
- Add temporary diagnostics for at most the first 16 actual EACCES syscall returns per boot. Each contains only the actual PID, syscall number and numeric errno. It reads no userspace buffer and preserves the original returned error.
- Preserve the exact A39 owner and original image profile, features, release settings, resource policy, deadlines, five scenarios and assertions.

Canonical diagnostic HEAD is `c42eccaf8b9b5a163d0c52b1a3c42466fe0f425b`, tree `6133f7825fd266f47c5546cb1220b25dba5361ff`. The earlier `07116475` diagnostic was superseded before any build or boot.

## Actual canonical execution — 2026-11-04

Durable desktop job `1a1a6fdf770-fc05-29c9` ran the original owner builder, original source-built kernel pipeline and complete five-boot runner. It reached terminal exit 1, with durable complete logs and no job timeout.

- Original owner Cargo build: exit 0, 3.812 s with the retained private warm target.
- Original release packaging: exit 0, 4.564 s. Owner ELF bytes remain exactly the original A39 image.
- Source-built OSDK: exit 0, 40.662 s.
- Product kernel: exit 0, 239.627 s; original pipeline validator passed.
- The independent final readback found both reviewed source roots at their exact clean HEAD/tree and rehashed the actual retained owner, kernel, QEMU records and raw serial logs.

| Scenario | Actual outcome |
| --- | --- |
| entropy-not-ready | PASS; refused before any role resumed |
| manifest-byte-mismatch | PASS; refused before any role resumed |
| truncated-snapshot | PASS; refused before any role resumed |
| steady-state-v1 | FAIL; QEMU 65 after 15.008 s, no timeout; 25,411 serial bytes |
| manager-exit-after-terminal-v1 | FAIL; QEMU 65 after 24.249 s, no timeout; 26,473 serial bytes |

The steady-state boot recorded `pid=2 syscall=42 errno=13` at guest 8.215 s. This is the Manager's connect call before the initial source state was created; the state disk preimage and postimage are identical. At that point the original Manager's only connection is the manager-launch endpoint. Source inspection identifies the publication race: Asterinas first creates the bound pathname with mode 0600; the original listener separately applies its group and 0660 permissions after binding the final visible name. A separate original-owner fix will publish the fully configured inode atomically and retain all connection deadlines.

The recovery-positive boot recorded no EACCES but returned `Unavailable` during initial activation, then the original Root lifetime/channel ended. That is a separate unresolved blocker. These logs do not establish a physical-material deadline failure. Both positive logs contain zero remaining per-Bio/IRQ INFO messages.

## Evidence

Retained root: `/data/trill-g2-c797-native-20261104-v1`.

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| source-review-c42-v1.json | `1eaca0494cadc84fd44fdb86419a2ca40dfe3c69a0415ff7fd0b851ce849e6a4` |
| owner-build-c42-v1/result.json | `09262eda5fdbe59ab301cbce9cab505bf51cf3e47e3615a958a34677b81683b1` |
| actual owner ELF | `6ce96a0785b2cbb51bb71fabb2973c1e04d93e213d56694b42b4d717ed55a454` |
| kernel-build-c42-v1/pipeline.json | `53e2d950eeb8fa23b069e98a220f85963950cf080434a7862e97cee156db42ce` |
| actual kernel ELF | `20e01606f9f6a87b9665986dbda1a271705a42c28607ee11d13e40857f46e6c1` |
| native-c42-v1/result.json | `3defd519ce9530fb29c4db1eb4b9a7e004649b04cf89dc3af445fc76c25345d2` |
| execution-chain-c42-v1.json | `3d4d8beeb81cc2af082498b896b6cf724d49d6e2f95982cf352b94b9f751b405` |
| native-c42-diagnostic-v1.json | `74ad0dc5d2218cb0b378632a1cd5b225fb6b7fb69c443490e56e0882ff70cb7a` |

The chain receipt contains the exact executed commands and all storage admissions. The preparation-only job `1a1a6f95c49-fc05-29b0` failed before canonical import/build because of an operational Python/JSON serialization mistake; its failure is preserved and is not a build result. The corrected launch imported only raw Git commit objects whose hashes exactly matched the published canonical SHAs.

Pinned nightly rustfmt and `git diff --check` passed for the two changed files. The native policy remains physical material 500 ms, guest 1 CPU / 512 MiB and 120 s per boot. The entropy refusal retains its original `max,-rdrand` CPU setting. Original native storage gates were retained, with additional concurrent Root disk reserve checks.

This diagnostic draft has not closed either positive scenario, the owner startup race, full G2 or production qualification.
